messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm out for a family thing starting Sun 18:00 PST through Mon 06:00 PST. I just realized our primary/secondary for that block are both flagged as unavailable (sam -> emergency, alex -> travel). Can someone take primary for Sun overnight? We already have a low-sev latency alert on hosted inference in us-west1 that popped a few mins ago, so would be good to coordinate handoff.

incident-bot: [ALERT] high p95 latency detected for /v1/generate (model: xlarge-redwood) in region us-west1. p95=920ms (>800ms threshold). Current state: firing. Page route: #oncall -> eng-oncall.

sam: sorry everyone — family emergency. I can't cover tonight. I'm paged and won't be online for the next ~12h. Really sorry for the timing.

alex: I can cover from 18:00-00:00 PST, but I have a meeting 00:00-02:00 and won't be able to respond then.

jon: I can take full primary for the window. I'll be on-call from 18:00->06:00 PST. I'll also own the live alert mitigation while I'm primary.

maya: Legend, thanks jon. Can you confirm you'll follow the inference latency runbook and escalate to infra if you see node GPU saturation? Link: <https://internal.redwood/runbooks/inference-latency|runbook — inference latency>

jon: Yep. Quick checklist I'll follow on first touch:
- confirm alert source (model, region, route)
- check autoscaler metrics and GPU load
- check KV cache hit rate and recent deploys
- throttle routing if necessary to force fallback to smaller model variant
- open bridge if customer-impacting or >15m sustained

jon: Reproducing key commands I use (posting here for whoever fills in later):
```
# check autoscaler / pods
kubectl get hpa -n inference
kubectl get pods -l app=serving -n inference -o wide
# tail logs for serving boxes with high latency
kubectl logs -n inference deployment/serving --tail 200 | grep "p95" -n
# check gpu util with prometheus query (grafana)
# prometheus: avg_over_time(gpu_util[5m]) by (instance)
```

jon: First mitigation I'm going to try at 18:05 — bump replica limit for us-west1 pool and temporarily route low-priority traffic to cheaper variant. If that doesn't bring p95 below 800ms in 10m, we'll open a bridge.

oncall-bot: Routing note: escalation policy applied. If primary doesn't acknowledge within 5 minutes, page secondary. If both fail, page infra-oncall.

alex: I'll stay reachable until midnight and can take over if jon needs to hand off earlier. If you open a bridge ping me @alex so I can join the bridge for the initial diagnosis.

maya: Thanks all. Jon — when you take primary please post a short handoff note at 06:00 with final actions and if any follow-ups remain. Also add the customer impact summary (estimated affected requests and duration) to the incident ticket.

jon: Will do. Also leaving a quick handoff template I'll paste at 06:00:
- shift_owner: jon
- incidents_handled: [inference-latency-us-west1]
- mitigation_steps: [scaled pool, reroute low-priority]
- customer_impact_estimate: ~2.1k requests 18:03-18:24, p95 peaked 920ms
- followups: verify autoscaler tuning and look at recent model rollout at 17:40

maya: Perfect. I'll update the oncall calendar so future overlap like this flags earlier. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: [INFO] alert transitioned to acknowledged by jon at 1767779400. p95 trending down to 640ms after routing change.

jon: confirmed — p95 back under 800ms after reroute and scaling. I'll monitor until 06:00 and post final summary at handoff. Thanks alex + maya.

maya: Awesome — thank you jon. Really appreciate the quick pickup. :handshake:
